title: ULTRACOMPACT 778 NM RUBIDIUM SECONDARY OPTICAL FREQUENCY STANDARD - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop an ultracompact, secondary, optical frequency reference based on a two-photon transition in Rb vapour at 778nm.Description:Ultra-stable miniature atomic clocks are being considered for space applications. The Rubidium two-photon transition secondary frequency standard has demonstrated interesting performance metrics with a further potential for ultra-low size, weight and power (SWaP) integration.Currently, such an approach is hindered by the lack of miniaturized laser sources with suitable power levels and spectral properties as well as a compact physics package design taking advantage of the full capabilities of the integrated photonics and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) gas cell technology platforms.This activity aims at exploiting these enabling technologies and developing a further concept of a compact high-performance atomic physics package for an ultra-compact secondary optical frequency standard. The goal of this activity is to provide a fractional frequency stability < 10 - 12 at 1 second integration time implemented using integrated photonic techniques.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Evaluate sources of integrated photonic laser systems delivering the wavelengths and the required spectral properties for the defined system approach. Develop Rb cell techniques and technologies targeting an ultracompact 778 nm rubidium secondary optical frequency standard using chip-scale photonic integration. Demonstrate the fractional stability performance achievable using the chosen chip-scale photonic approach. Evaluate chip-scale optical frequency combs with SiN Kerr comb techniques to provide an initial stabilized direct optical-RF link. Provide a packaging solution to maintain the preliminary performance achieved.NOTE: This activityis currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The finallist of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: RADIOISOTOPE THERMOELECTRIC GENERATOR THERMAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEM - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a passive thermal system to regulate the Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator temperature and to provide excess heat to the spacecraft/lander heat management system.Description: For exploration missions, there is a need (In situ resource utilization, deep space missions, long night survival...) to use efficient power generation systems as an alternative to solar panels. Europe is already engaged in developing a Radioisotope Heater Unit (RHU) and the next step is to develop bigger capabilities witha Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (RTG). As RTG is generating significant waste heat, there is an interest to reuse this heatand optimize the thermal control system, hence the whole system. Several thermal management systems with heat recovery are currently under study with the potential capability of receiving waste heat form RHU or RTG. However, interfacing with an RTG and regulatingits temperature is complex and requires a dedicated system for this unit. The goal of the activity is to develop a passive thermal system that regulates the temperature of the RTG and be able to provide excess heat to the spacecraft/lander heat management system viaa dedicated thermal interface. The RTG thermal system requires to operate with less than 5% of the electrical power generated bytheRTG. The heat recovery and the distribution of the RTG thermal energy would increase the overall efficiency of the system by more than 20%. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements consolidation - Technology trade off review - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard demonstrator - Validation testing of the breadboard demonstrator - Way forward for industrializationDeliverables: Breadboard, ReportProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators. title: JOINT IMPLEMENTATION OF SAT-3 AND COGNITIVE CLOUD COMPUTING IN SPACE (EOCOGNITIVELAB)
description: EOCognitiveLab brings together the evolution of the sat mission series and ESA's work on Cognitive Cloud Computing in Space for Earth Observation (3CS4EO). The activity is intended to demonstrate the added values unlocked by AI-enabled, cooperative Earth Observation capabilities across multiple heterogeneous?satellites?(including, event-based acquisition replanning, coordinated acquisitions), onboard processing and inter-satellite-link information exchange,?for selected end-to-end Earth Observation use cases, and to establish an in-orbit laboratory for autonomous, distributed and software-defined Earth Observation missions.?  The mission will be based on a cooperative two-satellite space segment, equipped with onboard computing capabilities, supported by ground processing, and an exploitation platform enabling data distribution and community access. In addition, EOCognitiveLab will leverage open inter-satellite-link interfaces and be designed to support future expansion through the federation of additional Earth Observation missions.? As an in-orbit laboratory, EOCognitiveLab will provide an open and expandable environment for additional in-orbit experimentation forESA Members, Associated and Cooperating States EO community. title: NON-BODY SOLID WASTE COMPACTION AND INHIBITION
description: Objective: To develop a breadboard demonstrating single-step waste inhibition and compaction and characterize cross-linked biodegradable materials compatible for this process.Description: Re-supply and waste management are critical components of crewed space exploration. The current waste management approach exposes the crew to (bio)safety risks during the temporary storage period and is unpractical in longer space missions. Generic waste compaction/inhibition technologies of mixed waste materials in space have been generally studied. However, despite promising results on the volume reduction performance, the physical characteristics of the product obtained allow for limited transformation of re-usable resources. To address this, the activity aims to develop a breadboard demonstrating single-step waste inhibition and compaction and characterize cross-linked biodegradable materials compatible for this process. Lastly, there is a benefit in defining new packaging materials, which are biodegradable in the conditions of identified recycling systems and withstand the proposed compaction and inhibition process. The activity includes the following tasks: - Review single-step waste inhibition/compaction methods compatible with resource recovery (e.g. water) and developed biodegradable materials - Trade-off and selection of integrated waste inhibition and compaction processes and compliant packaging/padding materials. - Design and assembly of a breadboard system for single-step waste inhibition and compaction - Test to validate selected single-step waste inhibition and compaction technological modifications and biodegradability of treated packaging material - Developed cross-linking agents to enhance the barrier properties of biodegradable packaging materials, while maintaining biodegradability and process compatibility - Test to validate biodegradability and intended use of developed packaging. - Define a roadmap for technology maturation for integration into an operational system.Deliverables: Breadboard, Report
